assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Reinstating the equality match, or dropping the expansion, leaves _finding_bullets empty while _open_rows_in_the_view returns three rows; the base arm shows exactly that at 6cc82823.
The expected texts come from the BENEATH fixture written by _store, not from the brief, so a brief carrying the wrong rows or over-collecting the ABOVE finding reddens.
A named-file review that still matches its package directory, or leaks a sibling finding, yields more than one bullet or the ABOVE text and reddens.
If _store_unreadable_paths or the None branch is removed the line reads 'Open findings already stored against the named paths: none.' and both assertions redden; the base arm shows that.

findings.text: The delivered manifest is a five-line stub that stops at the bare word NEXT: no commits, no tests line, no test_logs, no baseline_suite/after_suite, no landing. `crew check --manifest --run r-20261115T083000485371-qwnw-a-code-review-brief-carries-findings-under-its-paths` answers ok=false with 'status is complete but no commit is recorded', 'status is complete but no test result is recorded' and 'no delivery receipt was recorded, so the manifest must say `messages_received: none`'. Nothing in the delivered record ties commits a11bd1381a and 10e7b2f1aa to the 3-passed gate or to the base arm's two failures.

The passing arm's header names revision 6cc82823b5917cc458b5064ee49efb1cba97e093, the base revision, because it ran in the worktree before the fix was committed (log mtime 14:18:53, commit a11bd1381a authored 14:24:39); no gate log names a11bd1381a or 10e7b2f1aa, so the recorded receipt cannot be tied to the landed revision. The done_when's clause 'the tests run on all_debug' also has no evidence: every log in the run is a local worktree run.

This test file and the three production modules the fix edits (reckon/crew/plan_review.py, reckon/crew/findings.py, reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py) lie outside the node's declared write paths, which name only docs/evidence/fragments/queued-work-needs-no-workaround/qwnw-a-code-review-brief-carries-findings-under-its-paths.html and docs/figures/queued-work-needs-no-workaround/qwnw-a-code-review-brief-carries-findings-under-its-paths. The plan section names no write path, the run was fenced true and no dispatch grant widened it; docs/evidence/fragments/queued-work-needs-no-workaround/s22.html is out of scope by the same declaration although the done_when names it.

_finding_is_beneath re-implements at-or-beneath path containment that the repository already owns at reckon/crew/domain_rules.py:83 and reckon/crew/findings.py:1011, rather than extending either owner, so a change to containment semantics in domain_rules does not reach the brief.

The assertion that the brief's count equals the findings view's count is exercised only on a fixture with no sibling sharing the directory prefix: the view filters with a bare startswith at reckon/crew/findings.py:1102 while the brief matches on a path boundary, so a finding on reckon/subtle.py is counted by the view and not by the brief and the done_when's equality clause is not guarded in general.
